exposure: serum estradiol (E2) levels prior to progesterone administration
cohort: The study included 3857 frozen-thawed blastocyst transfer cycles, categorized into three groups based on serum estradiol (E2) levels prior to progesterone administration.
finding: High serum E2 levels prior to progesterone administration in artificial endometrial preparation (AEP) are associated with a decreased live birth rate, decreased clinical pregnancy rate, and increased pregnancy loss rate after frozen-thawed blastocyst transfer.
